title: Serving runtime weekly hodgepodge — May 4 2027
body:
Purpose:
Quick catch-all notes from this week’s serving-runtime syncs, experiments, and oncall handoffs. Intended to be readable by anyone ramping onto KV/batching/kernel topics; contains rough results, oddball findings, and explicit next steps (mostly action items, some open questions).

Highlights this week:
- Shipped a small kernel opt (temporal-slice prefetch) to staging; reduced 99th latency for short-chat workloads by ~6ms p99 in the micro-batch path. Patch: PR 1283 (see linked artifacts).
- Ran a 2-hour shadow run of the new KV-prefill shadowing mode against production traffic (read-only). Observed prefix hit-rate increase from 18% -> 24% in the 5–20 token window. Memory overhead was ~12% for the shard set we used.
- Microbatching heuristic A/B: heuristic A (latency-first) vs heuristic B (throughput-first) on dedicated machines. A maintained 5% lower p50 latency but reduced overall throughput by ~9%. B raised throughput by ~14% but increased tail latency.

Meeting notes (Wed 2027-05-05 10:00 serving-runtime weekly):
- Attendees: Asha, Marco, Priya, Ben, Yuki, Dev (oncall)
- Quick status round: Prefill shadowing experiment in prod shadows; kernel patch in staging; rollout blocked on perf regression in one quantized model.
- Ben: showed kernel flame graphs from new prefetch (temporal-slice). Hotspots moved from cudaMemcpy peaks to attention-kernel compute; suggests we are saturating compute now.
- Priya: KV hit-rate improvement is promising but noticed eviction churn on shard-3 under bursty traffic. Suspect eviction policy sensitivity to skew.
- Marco: microbatching A/B needs longer run; we are seeing coupling between batching window and GPU utilization that’s not linear. Need synthetic runs with controlled request inter-arrival distribution.
- Action: schedule a 4-hour synthetic load harness run Friday morning (owner: Marco).

Shadow run details and anomalies:
- Duration: 2 hours (Tue 2027-05-04 02:00–04:00 PDT).
- Traffic: 15% of production+replay (read-only); models: repr-13B/quant8 (staging flavor).
- Metrics: token-throughput stable, 99th latency on shadow path +3–5ms vs baseline for long-context requests (>512 tokens). Short-context improved.
- Memory: average per-gpu KV working set +12%, peak +18% (transient).
- Observed anomaly: one host (srv-rw-12) reported periodic GC spikes correlated with a background snapshot job. Snapshot timing overlapped with the shadow run — possible fluke.
- Note: eviction churn hypothesis — shard-3 experienced >2x active key turnover during one burst; need to capture per-key access patterns for that shard.

Kernel patch (temporal-slice prefetch) summary:
- Intention: prefetch upcoming KV blocks aligned to attention window boundaries to reduce cudaMemcpy jitter and overlapping memcpy/compute stalls.
- Implementation notes: added a light-weight lookahead that is aware of batching boundaries; falls back to legacy path if prefetch budget exceeded.
- Staging results: p50 improved ~2ms, p95 ~1.5ms, p99 ~6ms for small-generation flows (<=64 tokens). No functional regressions seen in unit tests.
- Risk: increased pressure on GPU memory for long-context flows; guarded by a configured prefetch budget.

Microbatching experiments (A vs B):
- Heuristic A (latency-first): small batch cutoff, aggressive early flush -> lower p50/p90, worse throughput.
- Heuristic B (throughput-first): builds batches for longer up to gpu fill target -> higher throughput, higher tail.
- Observed side-effect: Heuristic B increases staleness of token-level KV cache slightly which spikes divergence in a small percentage (~0.4%) of eval prompts (we saw small quality regressions on rerank tests).
- Decision: do not roll B to hosted until we can reconcile quality diffs; continue tuned rollout on Dedicated.

Oncall handoff and incidents:
- Wed 03:45 PDT: transient 504s on model repr-7B in us-west-2. Root cause: one autoscaler mis-evaluated GPU health due to telemetry gap (prometheus scrape failure), scaled down + immediate backfill which caused cold-kv storms.
- Mitigation: emergency fallback route enabled to a compatible smaller-replica variant (replica-compat-7b-fast). That restored traffic within 90s.
- Postmortem TODOs: (1) add guardrail to prevent simultaneous scale-down + rollout if kv warmup < threshold, (2) add synthetic scrape check in autoscaler path. Owners: Priya (1), Yuki (2).

Open questions / discussion items:
- Eviction policy: should we bias eviction to keep short-prefixes longer vs full sequences? Hypothesis: short-prefix retention improves latency for common short completions at small memory cost. (Discussion owner: Priya).
- Prefetch budget tuning: can we auto-tune budget per-model based on observed working set variance? (Owner: Asha).
- Microbatching quality drift: what are robust acceptance tests to catch small rerank/regression deltas before rollout? Proposal: expand eval set with noisy prompts and track top-k token overlap and rerank score distributions. (Owner: Marco + Research).

Action items (explicit):
- Marco: run 4-hour synthetic load harness Friday 05/07 08:00 PDT; collect per-shard access heatmaps and steady-state batch size distribution.
- Priya: capture eviction traces for shard-3 during reproduction window; attempt varying LRU window and assess churn. Due: 2027-05-09.
- Ben: land small follow-up to PR1283 to add telemetry counters for prefetch budget overflows. Due: 2027-05-06.
- Yuki: implement autoscaler synthetic scrape check and add guardrail to scale-down logic. Due: 2027-05-11.
- Asha: prototype auto-tune prefetch budget PoC (simulated workload) and share notebook. Due: 2027-05-14.

Quick notes to self / scribbles:
- Remember: check conformance of quantized kernels for repr-13B — micro-batching patterns expose deterministic corner-case in attention masking.
- Slack threads referenced during meeting: #serving-runtime, #perf-bench. Link copies in linked_artifacts.
- Consider adding small "prefill warmup" traffic generator for warm start tests in CI to catch cold-kv storms during autoscaler events.

Appendix: short metrics snapshot (end of shadow run):
- baseline p50/p95/p99 (short-chat): 8ms / 18ms / 42ms
- staging-with-prefetch p50/p95/p99 (short-chat): 6ms / 16.5ms / 36ms
- kv prefix hit-rate (5-20 tokens): baseline 18% -> shadow 24%
- batch size mean (heuristic A): 1.8 requests per batch; heuristic B: 3.6 requests per batch
- throughput delta (heuristic B vs baseline): +14% throughput, p99 delta +9ms

If anything above looks wrong / data inconsistent ping me (Asha) in #serving-runtime or add a comment in PR1283.

==== end of notes ====
